back: The part of a non-current asset's cost used up in a period, charged as an expense (a non-cash expense).
Wear and tear; obsolescence; passage of time; depletion.
(Cost − residual value) ÷ useful life in years.
Rate % × net book value at the start of the year (cost − depreciation so far).
Opening value + items bought − sale proceeds − closing value.
Cost less accumulated depreciation (Cambridge also says carrying amount).
Matching: spread the cost over the years that benefit; prudence: do not overstate profit or assets.

front: Which method suits vehicles, buildings and loose tools?
back: Vehicles: reducing balance. Buildings, leases, furniture: straight line. Loose tools, crockery, livestock: revaluation.
Charge only for the months owned: annual charge × months ÷ 12.
